head: 72c2c6891
summary: Two proven blockers. (1) #927 closes three doors that six db test files the lane never touched still drive: 33 cells go red on the post-0282 frontier, every one with the new retirement refusal as its error. (2) The retirement's own premise is false: clara._propose_adjustment_template_core is untouched by design and still mints a status='proposed' adjustment template, proven inside a rolled-back transaction; the path into it (clara.wake_establish_prepayment_schedule) is granted to clara_wake_interactive AND present in clara.wake_fn_allowlist, so after #927/#928/#929 a template can still be born that can never be signed, never be run, never be swept, and is never named by the plan advisory. Three further majors: the #909 advisory's self-exclusion by basis identity hides the total-overlap case, and this very rig carries clients with four live byte-identical-basis plans that warn about nothing; two concurrent sessions each creating an overlapping plan both see null; and the Adjustments tab still renders 'An adjustment run is due for X - Y' for real clients on this database with no act left anywhere. #908's yield wall itself survived every adversarial probe I could build (ten schedule shapes, single-period prepayment windows, leap February, the immutability chain, cross-caller token retention); its only defect is a fabricated citation baked into the shipped function body. Tenant isolation, rank floors, ACL and posture, lock order, migration idempotency, the frozen-workflow closure and parts parity all held.

gates_rerun_by_this_review.node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs: PASS - 312 frozen files, 55 use-workflow modules, 3 retired entries
gates_rerun_by_this_review.NOT re-run by this review: the Playwright walks (adjustments-retired-walk.spec.ts, the plans walk) and the whole apps/web unit suite

findings.title: 33 db cells in six test files the lane never touched go red on the post-0282 frontier, every one with the #927 retirement refusal as its error
findings.evidence: Run from packages/db with the full $GATES chain and PGHOST=127.0.0.1 PGPORT=55745 PGDATABASE=clara_l05: tests/x42-r10-p1-lineage.test.mjs 0 pass / 7 fail; tests/x42-r10-p1-recovery.test.mjs 0 pass / 1 fail; tests/x42-r11-lineage.test.mjs 0 pass / 18 fail; tests/f-a4-pr2a-wrapper.test.mjs 20 pass / 1 fail; tests/f-a4-pr2a-books.test.mjs 3 pass / 4 fail; tests/f-a4-pr2a-census.test.mjs 8 pass / 2 fail. Total 33 failures. Sample errors verbatim from the TAP output: fa4p2a.W1 'the door no longer opens the human floor', actual = the new retirement body (f-a4-pr2a-census.test.mjs:34 asserts the door still delegates to _propose_adjustment_template_core - 0282 replaced that delegation with a raise); fa4p2a.W35 / W35-mutant / W34 / W44 / W45-nulldigest error 'clara.propose_adjustment_template is retired (#927)...' or 'clara.sign_adjustment_template is retired (#927)...'; x42.r10p1a..r10p1h, x42.r11a..r11i, x42.r12a..r12f, x42.r13a..r13b error 'clara.run_adjustment_manual is retired (#927)...'. The lane's #927 report claims 'The eight x42-adj db batteries ... stay green' and lists only x42-adjustments, x42-adj-due, x42-adjustments-stale, x42-adj-canon, x42-adj-reads, x42-adj-period-double, x42-pair, x42-pair-correction; the six files above drive the same three closed doors and were left untouched. No preintegration gate covers them - adjustment-template-doors-retired-preintegration-gate.mjs only quiets a MISSING 0282, never a present one. (x42-0045-b2-upgrade.test.mjs also calls all three but SKIPs as destructive and re-migrates only 0042->0045, so it is unaffected.)
findings.required_fix: Retarget the six files at the retired shape the way the eight x42-adj batteries were - insertTemplateRaw for the fixture, run_adjustment_occurrence for the poster, and for f-a4-pr2a-census.test.mjs:34/:60 a rewritten W1/W2 that no longer asserts the door delegates to the core or opens the human floor. If that is genuinely outside #927, say so in the report and file it: the wave cannot merge a branch whose db suite is 33 cells red.

findings.title: A 0045 adjustment template can still be BORN after all three retirement migrations: the agent-lane propose core is untouched and still reachable, and the row it mints can never be signed, run, swept or warned about
findings.evidence: PROVEN inside a transaction I rolled back, on clara_l05 at 0283: begin; select clara._propose_adjustment_template_core(jsonb_build_object('firm',<firm>,'actor',<user>,'client_id',<client>,'wake_kind','close_prep','task_id',gen_random_uuid()), <client>, 'ADV927 agent-lane probe', 'monthly', date '2026-07-01', null, false, <two balanced lines>, 'adv probe', <fresh op_key>, null, null, null) returned {"status":"proposed","template_id":"757d8a18-57cb-4325-a2c6-d2591ca75e90","content_hash":"e165ae0f..."}, and select count(*) from clara.adjustment_templates where name='ADV927 agent-lane probe' read 1 row at status='proposed'; rolled back. The path is live at the DB level, not theoretical: clara.wake_establish_prepayment_schedule(uuid,uuid,text,text,text,jsonb,text) is granted {clara_fn_owner, clara_wake_interactive}, its body calls clara._agent_prepayment_schedule_core, and that core is the only caller of _propose_adjustment_template_core; clara.wake_fn_allowlist still carries (wake_kind='close_prep', function_name='wake_establish_prepayment_schedule'). Migration 0282's own header names this and steps around it: '...the OLD propose door's own former callee (still the agent-lane prepayment limb's entrance, 0140:1232 -- untouched, and still reachable through clara._agent_prepayment_schedule_core, which this file does not go near)'. The consequence is exactly what 0282's live-template guard exists to prevent, in its own words: 'a proposed row could never be signed again ... either shape would be this file silently orphaning a schedule a firm is still relying on'. After #927 sign_adjustment_template refuses; after #928 packages/runtime/lib/reconciler-adjustments.mjs is deleted so clara.run_adjustment_occurrence is never called; after #929 the live prosrc of clara._plan_overlap_warning contains neither 'adjustment_template_overlap' nor 'clara.adjustment_templates', so the row is never named by the advisory either. The only containment today is clara.wake_engine_sources.enabled = false for 'close_prep' - a parked feature flag, not a closed door, and unparking close_prep is a product goal.
findings.required_fix: Either close _propose_adjustment_template_core / _agent_prepayment_schedule_core with the same typed refusal (or reroute the agent limb at clara.create_prepayment_schedule, 0223's plan-lane door), or delete the clara.wake_fn_allowlist row and revoke clara_wake_interactive's EXECUTE on wake_establish_prepayment_schedule, in a migration this lane owns. If the owner rules it out of scope, the three reports and #683's blueprint-drift lines must say in one sentence that the 0045 lane is retired EXCEPT for the parked agent prepayment limb, so nobody unparks close_prep into a retired lane.

findings.title: The sibling-plan advisory's self-exclusion by basis identity hides the WORST overlap, and the estate this rig models produces that shape four plans at a time - not the 'coincidence' 0281's header claims
findings.evidence: Measured on clara_l05: select p.client_id, r.basis_digest, count(*) from clara.accounting_plans p join clara.accounting_plan_revisions r on r.plan_id=p.id and r.superseded_at is null where p.status in ('active','paused') group by 1,2 having count(*)>1 returns many clients at count 4. Driven for c9c86bf5-509e-42e6-b9d0-e29057ffd6ef: live_plans=4, distinct_bases=1, and clara._plan_overlap_warning(<that client>, <that basis>) answers NULL. The same call with one key nudged (a different memo, the same two account codes) answers the full four-entry accounting_plan_overlap payload - so the arm works, and it is the r.basis is distinct from p_basis self-exclusion that swallows the exact case a human most needs told (total overlap). 0281's header calls this 'accepted' because 'two schedules an accountant authored with byte-identical bases ... is a coincidence this estate has never produced in practice'; the estate's own migrated-and-seeded rig produces it for most clients that have plans at all. Cross-client isolation is sound: the same nudged basis against a different client (d7e9ce2f-...) named only that client's own plan.
findings.required_fix: Exclude the row being evaluated by IDENTITY, not by value: widen clara._plan_overlap_warning to take the plan id the caller just wrote (all three callers already hold it - create_accounting_plan's v_plan, revise_accounting_plan's p.id, _accrual_plan_core's own insert) and self-exclude on p.id is distinct from p_self. If 'the three plan-creating doors ... unchanged' forbids that here, the accepted-limitation paragraph in 0281 and 0283 must be re-measured against this evidence and the residual filed, because the justification it currently gives is falsified.

findings.title: Two sessions creating overlapping plans concurrently both get NULL - the 'warning depends on creation order' defect #909 was filed over survives at the concurrency seam
findings.evidence: Driven with two real pg connections against clara_l05. Both BEGIN; session A inserts a plan plus its live revision on a brand-new account-code pair (ZZ909RACE / ZZ909RACEB) with memo 'alpha'; session B inserts its own on the same codes with memo 'beta' - a DIFFERENT basis, so ADV-L05-03's self-exclusion is not what is at work. Baseline before either insert: clara._plan_overlap_warning(<client>, <that basis>) = null. A then calls the advisory and sees null; B calls it and sees null. After A COMMITs, B - still inside its own transaction, READ COMMITTED - re-reads and now sees {"kind":"accounting_plan_overlap","templates":[{"name":"RACE alpha",...}]}, but B has already returned its own create receipt to its caller. Two overlapping plans land with neither human warned. Both fixtures were removed afterwards: clara.accounting_plans back to 544 rows, accounting_plan_revisions to 629, zero rows whose basis mentions ZZ909RACE. #909's own filing says 'the warning itself may not fire depending on creation order'; the sibling arm fixes the sequential case and leaves the concurrent one.
findings.required_fix: State the concurrency window explicitly in the ticket report and in 0281/0283's header (an advisory computed inside the creating transaction cannot see an uncommitted sibling), or take the client-level advisory lock this estate already uses for exactly this class of question - clara.retire_adjustment_template's pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(p_client::text)) - in the three plan-creating doors so two creations serialise. Do not leave the report asserting the advisory 'names every other live plan' without the caveat.

findings.title: The retired Adjustments tab still tells a firm an adjustment run is DUE, and after #927 plus #928 there is no act anywhere that can satisfy it
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/registers/adjustments-register.tsx keeps {gov.data ? <AdjustmentRunDueBanner due={gov.data.due} /> : null} - the diff removes Propose/Sign/Run-now and adds the retirement StateBanner but leaves the due banner untouched. apps/web/components/registers/adjustment-run-due-banner.tsx renders 'An adjustment run is due for {start} - {end}.' on due.due, and on reason='all_blocked' renders 'Every live template's next period is blocked - see the run history below.' That state is reachable on real data now: select t.client_id, clara._adjustment_run_due_core(t.client_id, c.firm_id) from (select distinct client_id from clara.adjustment_templates where status='live') t join clara.clients c on c.id=t.client_id where (clara._adjustment_run_due_core(...)->>'due')::boolean returns rows - e.g. client b0f7e9c6-d314-4574-ab22-4318af0eb677 {"due":true,"template_id":"9256f0f7-f68e-4add-bdb4-d4446b993d1f","period_start":"2026-06-01","period_end":"2026-06-30"}. clara.adjustment_run_due is still granted to clara_authenticated and apps/web/lib/registers/adjustments.ts:206 still calls it. Run-now is gone (#927), clara.run_adjustment_manual refuses (#927), and reconciler-adjustments.mjs is deleted so clara.run_adjustment_occurrence is never called again (#928): the banner asserts an obligation the product can no longer discharge. The firm #927's D6 reading protects - 'a firm that ran this lane before today must still be able to read its history' - is exactly the firm that sees this.
findings.required_fix: Either suppress the due banner on the retired tab (render the retirement notice in its place, or branch it on retired) or give the banner retired copy that names the successor instead of an act. One web string plus one branch, inside #927/#928's own scope; leaving it ships a screen that says something is owed and offers nothing.

findings.title: 0282's live-template guard is unsatisfiable on any estate that holds a non-retired template - including this lane's own database after the lane's own tests, so a #957 redo or a re-apply is now refused
findings.evidence: The guard is select count(*) from clara.adjustment_templates where status <> 'retired' -> raise CLR10 if non-zero. Measured on clara_l05 now: 491 non-retired rows (144 live + 5 proposed at first measurement, more since). The lane's own retargeted fixtures put them there - insertTemplateRaw in x42-adj-helpers.mjs and plan-overlap-sibling-arm.test.mjs's 'Rig overlap template' / 'Rig 929 combo template' INSERT status='live' and status='proposed' rows directly and never clean them up. Confirmed by running the guard's exact statement inside a transaction I rolled back: NOTICE '0282 PRESTATE WOULD REFUSE: 491 non-retired adjustment_templates row(s) on this database right now'. The lane's #927 report records having had to retire ten stray rows by hand before the first apply - the same collision one migration earlier. On hosted the guard rests on a census taken 2026-09-18; on release day it is a live gate, not a fact. The remedy is sound: clara._tf_adjustment_template_transition admits proposed->retired and clara.retire_adjustment_template back-fills signed_by/signed_at for a never-signed row (both read off the live catalog). A true from-scratch chain passes vacuously - nothing under packages/db/seeds inserts clara.adjustment_templates.
findings.required_fix: Put in the #927 report and the release runbook that 0282 must be preceded by a fresh select count(*) from clara.adjustment_templates where status <> 'retired' on hosted and, if non-zero, a retire-by-hand pass; and note that a redo of 0282 on any lane database that has run the x42 batteries will be refused, so the integrator's from-scratch proof is the one that has to carry this migration.

findings.title: 0280 cites clara.revise_accrual_adjustment three times - including inside the function body it ships - and that function exists nowhere in the catalog
findings.evidence: select p.oid::regprocedure::text from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='clara' and p.proname ~ 'accrual' on clara_l05 lists create_accrual_adjustment, create_accrual_adjustment_for, get_accrual_adjustment, list_accrual_adjustments and the private helpers - there is no revise_accrual_adjustment. grep -rn revise_accrual_adjustment packages/db/migrations/*.sql matches only 0280, at lines 14, 31 and 265; line 265 sits inside the create or replace function clara._assert_plan_schedule body, so the fabricated citation is now permanent prosrc on every estate this migration reaches. The supporting claim is also mis-aimed: the header says the two doors call _assert_accrual_schedule_yields 'at 0222:1182/1283'; measured, the two callers are clara.create_accrual_adjustment (granted clara_authenticated) and clara.create_accrual_adjustment_for (granted clara_runtime, the OBO door), so a reviewer reading the header would not learn that the runtime door also keeps the accrual token. The behaviour is correct either way; the record is not.
findings.required_fix: Correct the three citations in a follow-up migration comment or in the ticket report (AGENTS.md rule 6: no evidence, no claim), naming clara.create_accrual_adjustment_for as the second caller. Do not leave 'revise_accrual_adjustment' as an anchor a later reader will chase.

findings.title: SURGERY 5 makes every retargeted x42 battery mint its template by direct INSERT, so the lineage, replaces and FY-freshness validation those rows used to carry is no longer exercised anywhere
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/x42-adj-helpers.mjs: liveTemplate() now calls insertTemplateRaw(), a superuser INSERT that computes content_hash through clara._adj_canon_lines/_adj_template_hash and sets signed_by/signed_at by hand. The row shape is faithful - I confirmed the constraint trigger t_adjustment_templates_lineage_root is AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE so lineage is still enforced on the raw insert, and t_adjustment_templates_transition is BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE only, so the helper's claim holds - but propose_adjustment_template's p_replaces lineage rules and sign_adjustment_template's template_fy_stale re-derivation now have no live caller and no cell. The #927 report describes x42-adj-period-double's cd6 'retire + re-propose' as needing 'no special handling once liveTemplate itself stopped calling propose'; that scenario no longer tests a re-proposal, only a second raw row.
findings.required_fix: Record in the #927 report which validations lost their last exercise (p_replaces lineage, template_fy_stale, the propose-time period-overlap advisory) so #683's census can retire their specs deliberately rather than by attrition.

findings.title: In-code comments still describe the 0045 lane as live after #929 retired it
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/(firm)/clients/[clientId]/plans/page.tsx:10 still reads '...registers?tab=adjustments, which is the LIVE 0045 adjustment-template lane - a different...'; apps/web/app/(firm)/clients/[clientId]/accounting/adjustments/page.tsx:14 reads 'That tab is the 0045 PLAN lane'. Both were true before this lane and are false after it. Not a defect, but worth recording: the tab itself IS still reachable, so the new retirement notice does render for a human - apps/web/lib/navigation/tree.ts:382-386 states that #640 repointed the sidebar row to /clients/:id/plans while the register 'stays exactly where it was, reachable at registers?tab=adjustments through the workbench's own SectionTabs'.
findings.required_fix: One-line edits in the two page headers, or a line in the #929 report handing them to #683 alongside the ARCHITECTURE.md:500 blueprint-drift line.

adversarial_probes_that_found_nothing: Tenant isolation of the new sibling arm: clara._plan_overlap_warning(<client A>, <basis matching client B's plan>) named only client A's own plans; the arm filters p.client_id = p_client, and clara.accounting_plans.client_id/firm_id are both NOT NULL with a composite FK from the revisions table.

Rank floors and posture: _plan_overlap_warning and _assert_plan_schedule are both {clara_fn_owner=X/clara_fn_owner} only, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=clara,pg_temp, STABLE and IMMUTABLE respectively; the three closed doors kept exactly {clara_fn_owner, clara_authenticated}, SECURITY DEFINER, the same search_path and VOLATILE - measured live off pg_proc, not read off the tails.

Existence oracle in the retirement refusal: all three closed doors raise before touching any argument, any table or _human_ctx, so a caller from another firm, a viewer and an admin all receive the identical CLR10 adjustment_template_lane_retired; the refusal carries no template id, client or status.
Duplicate sibling entries: ix_plan_revisions_live is a UNIQUE partial index on (plan_id) WHERE superseded_at IS NULL, so the sibling arm's join can never double-count a plan.

Self-exclusion soundness for the ordinary case: create_accounting_plan (prosrc lines 110/115), revise_accounting_plan (110/121) and _accrual_plan_core (61/65) all insert p_basis VERBATIM and pass the SAME jsonb to the advisory, so the row just written is always excluded and a plan never warns about itself.

#908 false refusals: probed ten schedule shapes plus every single-period prepayment window create_prepayment_schedule derives (v_from/v_to = first/last period_end, always month ends). 1-period Jan, 1-period non-leap Feb 28, 1-period leap Feb 29 2028, 1-period 30-day Apr, 2-period, 12-period and a single-day accrual on its own due day all yield TRUE; only genuinely non-performing windows refuse (monthly last-day Jan 1..Jan 30, monthly dom=28 Feb 1..Feb 27, quarterly dom=15 Jan 20..Apr 10, monthly dom=1 Jan 2..Jan 31). Early termination is unaffected: clara.end_accounting_plan(p_plan,p_reason,p_op_key) never reaches _assert_plan_schedule.

Volatility honesty of the new IMMUTABLE call chain: _assert_plan_schedule -> _accrual_schedule_yields -> _plan_due_events -> _plan_due_nth / _plan_due_index_on_or_before / _plan_reversal_date are all provolatile='i'; no now() or timezone read enters the wall, so Asia/Kuala_Lumpur drift cannot move a refusal.

Lock order: neither #908 nor #909/#929 adds a lock; the sibling arm is a plain MVCC read that cannot block on _plan_admit_occurrence's FOR UPDATE over clara.accounting_plans, and the three closed doors now take no lock at all.

Idempotency under replay: the three closed doors ignore p_op_key entirely and reserve nothing, so a replay with the same key and a different payload gets the identical refusal and writes nothing; operation-census.test.mjs is green.
From-scratch safety of 0282's data guard: nothing under packages/db/seeds or packages/db/scripts inserts clara.adjustment_templates, so a 0001->0283 chain satisfies the guard vacuously.

Runtime retirement completeness: nothing in the repo imports reconciler-adjustments.mjs, reconcileAdjustmentRuns, the runtime adjustmentRunDue, or reads swept.adjOk; check-frozen-workflows.mjs and check-parts-parity.mjs are both green after the re-fingerprinted spread tuples.

i18n: the removed keys (linesEditor, proposeTemplate, signTemplate, runNow) were all under the Adjustments namespace and nothing references them - the surviving JournalsWorkbench.linesEditor and StaffAdvances.linesEditor are different namespaces. All three forms' overlap copy was rewritten, and no 'recurring adjustment template' string survives in an advisory.

Deploy skew on the web types: template_id -> plan_id is type-only; no component reads either field (the three forms read only overlap_warning.templates.map(x => x.name)), so a stale client build against an older server renders the same text.
